gate_vs_route_relationship.quoted_gate: spec.md:106 (41fa7698, blob 2cbbdf99): 'Full private HTTP readback SHALL remain blocked until a source-only audience contract that NAMES THE READBACK AUDIENCE, its concrete caller, and its authentication story exists; the envelope-carriage audience contract admitted by D12 (2026-09-15) is NOT that contract and SHALL NOT be read as releasing this gate.' Restated at spec.md:122 and inside the D12 requirement block at spec.md:133 ('SHALL NOT be read as satisfying the readback gate above merely because it is a source-only audience contract').
gate_vs_route_relationship.literal_scope_of_the_gate: Read in full context (spec.md:96-133), this gate sits inside the 'Private source replay and AcceptContract producer' and 'Full contract and remaining market are source-only' requirements, which govern the JOURNAL-PRIVATE envelope (`ICampaignJournalEnvelope.sourcePrivate`, D12) and its wire narrowing via `envelopeOf`. The gate's own words -- 'a source-only audience contract... for the readback' -- describe a NOT-YET-BUILT surface: no route in the repository today reads `sourcePrivate` back out over HTTP (confirmed by the P0b review's item 1 enumeratedPaths and by this session's own surface inventory above finding zero `sourcePrivate` references outside `campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts` and its tests).
gate_vs_route_relationship.does_GET_id_violate_the_letter: NO, not literally. `GET /api/campaigns/:id` reads the `campaigns` table row (`SerializedCampaign.body.contractMarket`), a pre-journal, pre-D12 data model that predates every commit in the P0b/P1 stack and that no commit in the stack touches (confirmed: `git diff b7d650997 ac3481b3f --stat` -- not re-run in this pass, but the P0b review already confirmed the 6-file P0b stack diff excludes this route, and 6.2a/6.2b's own task text below confirms P1 does not touch it either). The 'full private HTTP readback' the gate names is specifically a readback OF THE JOURNAL-PRIVATE FIELD, which no route attempts.
gate_vs_route_relationship.does_GET_id_violate_the_spirit: YES, materially. D12/D13's own audience statement (spec.md:125, campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:6-7) is: 'their audience is the source instance's own server process and its persisted `SerializedCampaign` record.' The private envelope's baseline IS defined as a byte-identical capture of that same `SerializedCampaign.body` (`ICampaignSourceBaseline.sourceRecordBody`, campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:57-58). Building an airtight narrowing boundary around the JOURNAL copy of that data while the PLAINTEXT SOURCE of that same data is already retrievable, unauthenticated, by any caller who can reach the host process is a distinction without a difference for an attacker: today, and BEFORE 6.2 ships, `campaign.contractMarket` and `campaign.missions[*]` (full contract detail, since `acceptContractOffer` already writes full detail into `campaign.missions` client-side, per campaignCommandActions.ts:454-493) already reach the wire via this route on every existing single-player campaign. The private-envelope work secures a second copy of the data while the first copy stands open.
gate_vs_route_relationship.is_this_a_pre_existing_local_single_user: NOT SUPPORTED BY THE CODE. The project is not a single-user local-only app in the sense that would make an unauthenticated HTTP surface benign: (1) a real cryptographic player-identity/auth system exists and is live (`src/lib/multiplayer/server/auth.ts`, Ed25519 token verification, 'Wave 2 of Phase 4'); (2) four sibling routes in the exact same directory (`commands.ts`, `grants.ts`, `replica-sync.ts`, `rewind-preview.ts`) already gate on it; (3) the project supports GM+2-player co-op over room codes and network-reachable guest sessions (per project history and `roomCodeGuestHydration.ts`, `CampaignSessionParticipantStore`), meaning the host's HTTP server is, by the feature's own design, reachable by parties other than the single owning device. There is no design.md or proposal.md language anywhere in this change (grepped for 'localhost', '0.0.0.0', 'LAN', 'single-user', 'trusted network' -- no hits) asserting that campaign CRUD routes are exempt from the auth model applied to commands/grants/replica-sync/rewind-preview. The most defensible reading is: this route predates the co-op/auth work entirely (it is annotated `@spec add-campaign-persistence/...` and `@spec design-campaign-authority-and-sync/design.md (D2)`, i.e. the OLDER single-player persistence spec, not the newer multiplayer-auth one) and was never revisited when `authenticateRequest` was introduced for the sibling routes -- an oversight of scope, not a considered decision.

a_spec_amendment.description: Amend spec.md's readback-gate language (currently scoped only to a hypothetical journal-private HTTP readback) to explicitly name the PRE-EXISTING `SerializedCampaign`/`contractMarket` CRUD surface as within its concern, since D12's own baseline IS that record's body.
a_spec_amendment.verdict: NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE. Documents the gap precisely (closes the definitional loophole a future reader could exploit -- 'D12 only covers journal payloads' -- as OB-2 itself already warns), but a spec amendment does not close the live, already-reachable route.

b_route_auth_guard.description: Add `authenticateRequest` (+ an appropriate authorization check -- likely 'is a participant in this campaign's session', mirroring `campaignActivityRoute`'s 403 'not a participant' gate, or `isActiveCampaignSeat` where a co-op session exists, falling back to 'is the source device's own request' for solo campaigns with no session) to GET/PUT/DELETE on `[id].ts`, and to `adopt.ts`. `index.ts`'s summary-only response and `redeem.ts`'s token-gated create are lower priority (index leaks nothing sensitive; redeem already has a distinct auth story).
b_route_auth_guard.verdict: THE MINIMAL CORRECT FIX. Reuses an existing, already-battle-tested primitive (`authenticateRequest`) rather than inventing a new authorization abstraction; closes the actually-reachable leak; is architecturally symmetric with the 4 sibling routes that already do this. Estimated small (~30-60 changed lines per route plus tests) -- NOT sized in this session, flagged as a separate scoped task, not part of 6.2a/6.2b/6.4's own line budget.

gate_vs_route_relationship.can_P1_be_admitted_before_OB2_is_resolve: YES, admission is not technically blocked. 6.2a and 6.2b are scoped entirely to `campaignCommandPipeline.ts`, `campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts` (already merged), `campaignCommandActions.ts`, and `pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts` (already authenticated) -- none of which touch, widen, or depend on `[id].ts`'s GET/PUT/DELETE handlers. 6.2b does not change what `GET /api/campaigns/:id` returns; it changes WHO writes the compact ledger entry (server vs. client) for one mutation the route already exposes today, pre-6.2, via the existing client-side `acceptContractOffer` + debounced whole-envelope PUT. So 6.2a/6.2b do not make OB-2 worse and are architecturally independent of its fix. RECOMMENDATION: admit 6.2a/6.2b now, but raise the route-auth-guard task in parallel with an explicit note that it should land before (or very soon after) any future 'P1 is fully done' claim, since the private-envelope investment's value proposition depends on it.

6.4_exposure_concrete.the_two_counters: Confirmed two independent, un-bridged CAS tokens: (1) `SerializedCampaign.version`/`baseVersion` on the `campaigns` table, guarded by `CampaignPersistenceService.saveCampaign`'s `db.transaction` (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:103-131, `if (baseVersion !== currentVersion) return conflictFromStoredRow(...)`) and used by the client's debounced whole-envelope PUT (`useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts`, per the client-spec-delta evidence); (2) the journal stream revision (`expectedRevision`/`priorEvents.length`) used by `campaignCommandPipeline.ts`'s `executeCampaignCommand` (:326-330, :360-364) and returned in the `/commands` response's `head`.
6.4_exposure_concrete.what_breaks_on_the_next_auto_save_withou: Once 6.2b lands, a committed AcceptContract writes the source `campaigns` row's `missions`/`contractMarket` fields SERVER-SIDE (per 6.2b's own text: 'the source record's mission and reduced market come from 6.1's contract-only replay fold applied to the SAME commit'), which necessarily advances that row's `version`/`baseVersion` on the server WITHOUT the client's in-memory `baseVersion` knowing about it. The client's Zustand store still holds the PRE-acceptance `ICampaign` (per 6.2b: 'the client SHALL NOT also apply locally' on the committed path, and has no post-acknowledgement refresh path -- task 6.4's own text: 'the client's rendered ICampaign has no post-acknowledgement refresh path (the cache requirement covers LOAD-time validation only)'). The VERY NEXT debounced auto-save the client fires for ANY unrelated mutation (e.g. hiring a pilot) will PUT with the STALE `baseVersion`, and `CampaignPersistenceService.saveCampaign` will return a 409 conflict (`conflictFromStoredRow`) -- or, if `sourceReplayFence` (task 6.1, still unbuilt) is in place by then, a `sourceReplayFence` refusal instead of a plain conflict.
